ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act; the Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter on Yuhan Hoesa; and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, as amended) govern AML/CFT, customer due diligence, beneficial ownership identification, and foreign-investor reporting obligations. Korea maintains no public UBO register; beneficial-owner information is reported to licensed financial institutions and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the 25-percent ownership and control-based threshold rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Ultimate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The companies registration authority in the foreign shareholder jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path for Hague Apostille states: notarize the document, obtain an apostille from the designated competent authority, then obtain a sworn Korean translation; do not add consular legalization. Parallel path for non-Hague states: authenticate the public document at the local foreign ministry, legalize it at the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate with consular jurisdiction, then obtain a sworn Korean translation; do not use an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The companies registration authority or tax authority in the foreign shareholder jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague state: apostille from the designated competent authority after notarization, then certified Korean translation; consular legalization is not used. Non-Hague state: foreign-ministry authentication followed by consular legalization at the Korean embassy/consulate, then certified Korean translation; apostille is not used. The two paths are exclusive and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney Authorizing Korean Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The board of directors of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify the extract of board minutes, notarize the officers signatures, and then use either the apostille path for Hague states or the consular legalization path for non-Hague states, followed by a certified Korean translation. Never combine apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Korean-Language Articles of Association of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The incorporators and a Korean notary public at the competent district notary office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: This is a domestic Korean-origin charter; it is executed and notarized in the Republic of Korea. No Hague apostille and no consular legalization are required for use within Korea. If later used abroad, the apostille path would apply for foreign users, never consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter of the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The relationship bank of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank must countersign the letter, the countersignature is notarized, then apostilled in Hague states or legalized by the Korean consulate in non-Hague states, followed by certified Korean translation. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and never applied sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and major counterparties must be screened before incorporation and at bank onboarding against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the European Union and United Kingdom consolidated financial sanctions lists, and the Republic of Korea autonomous financial sanctions and restricted trade lists administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. Politically exposed persons must be identified through a risk-based methodology covering domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates, with mandatory senior-management approval for high-risk relationships, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, ongoing transaction monitoring, adverse media screening, and enhanced due diligence for jurisdictions with strategic AML deficiencies. Despite the bank-assigned Low_Risk_Standard tier, the screening protocols remain mandatory.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1001, as amended), notably Articles 172, 175, 289, 290, 292, 303, 317, 329, 330, 344, 345, 355, 386, 388, 434 and 530; Medical Devices Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 17558), Articles 9, 10 and 11.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry Office of the judicial district of the principal corporate domicile; for the expected Seoul headquarters, the registry authority is the Seoul Central District Court Registry Division, with online filing accepted at the Supreme Court of Korea I-Court e-filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration Application for Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (Designated Form), accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital subscription deposit certificate, corporate seal impression and officers' acceptance letters.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act; the law does not prescribe a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the incorporators must demonstrate that the shares subscribed have been fully paid into a blocked escrow account at a licensed Korean commercial bank, evidenced by a bank-issued capital deposit certificate attached to the court registration application. A working capital of at least KRW 10,000,000 is market practice to facilitate corporate account opening and vendor contracts. In-kind contributions must be verified by a court-appointed inspector's report under Article 314.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE ORGANIZERS AND INITIAL BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (YUHAN HOESA), REGISTERED OFFICE: [FULL ADDRESS], REPUBLIC OF KOREA. The organizers and initial directors, acting as the inaugural board of directors of the Company, held an extraordinary organizational meeting at the registered office on [DATE] at [TIME]. Written notice of the meeting having been unanimously waived by all persons entitled to receive notice, and a quorum of all directors being present throughout, the meeting was duly convened and proceeding. The following resolutions, having been read, discussed and unanimously adopted, are hereby recorded. 1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL. The board acknowledged the subscribers named in the Articles of Incorporation and confirmed that all authorized and issued common shares, totaling [NUMBER] shares, have been fully subscribed by the persons listed in Annex I. The board accepted the capital deposit certificate issued by [BANK NAME] evidencing that the full subscription price of the shares, being at least the amount required to comply with Article 329 and Article 330 of the Korean Commercial Act, was paid into the blocked escrow account established in the Company's reserved name. The board directed that subscription proceeds remain undistributed until the Court Registry completes the incorporation registration, and that the deposit certificate be attached to these minutes for filing with the Registry Office. 2. APPOINTMENT AND ELECTION OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The board unanimously appointed [DIRECTOR A] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [DIRECTOR B] as Chief Financial Officer and Accounting Director, and [DIRECTOR C] as Director of Legal Affairs and Company Secretary. Each appointee, being present, accepted the office and confirmed their capacity to act under Chapter IV of the Korean Commercial Act, including their fiduciary duty of care and loyalty. Each officer shall serve until the next annual general meeting or until successors are duly elected and qualified. 3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The board resolved that the registered principal office and statutory seat of the Company shall be at the address stated above, and that such address shall be shown in all official contracts and government filings. The board authorized the Representative Director to enter into a lease or service agreement for the registered office and to present the relevant proof to the registry upon request. 4. BANKING AND FINANCIAL AUTHORIZATION. The board authorized the opening of corporate operating, deposit and foreign currency accounts at [BANK NAME] (SWIFT: [SWIFT CODE]), and authorized the Representative Director, acting alone, to sign for ordinary banking transactions, including deposits, disbursements, and wire transfers. However, any transaction exceeding USD 100,000, any equipment purchase, and any import or export letter of credit relating to ECG patient monitor components shall require the joint signature of the Representative Director and the Company Secretary or Chief Financial Officer. The board approved the corporate seal and resolved that the Representative Director keep custody thereof. 5. REGULATORY FILING AUTHORIZATION. The board authorized the filing of the incorporation registration application with the competent Court Registry Office, the business registration with the National Tax Service, and the medical device manufacturing establishment license application with the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. Such filings may be executed by the Representative Director or by any duly appointed legal or licensed administrative agent. 6. GENERAL PROVISIONS. The board authorized payment of all incorporation expenses, taxes and registration fees, and instructed that the minutes of the organizational meeting be signed by the chair and the secretary and maintained in the corporate minute book available to shareholders and auditors. The foregoing resolutions were adopted unanimously and without objection. The meeting was duly adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation through the Court Name Search System
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea I-Court online name reservation portal and the local Court Registry Office of the intended head office district.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the I-Court e-filing system using the authorized agent's certificate or the attorney's digital certificate. Submit a name applicability search using one to four candidate names for a Yuhan Hoesa. The system will compare the submitted names against the registry of existing companies and report identical or deceptively similar matches. If a name is available, complete the online reservation request, pay the nominal reservation fee, and download the reservation certificate. This certificate is valid for six months and must be printed, signed and submitted to the notary public and eventually attached to the incorporation registration dossier. The name must include the expression Yuhan Hoesa to indicate limited liability. No manufacturing activity may commence until the reservation certificate is obtained, although pre-incorporation escrow banking may be initiated under the reserved name.
required_dossiers: Authorization letter or power of attorney for the filing agent
Digital certificate of the attorney or licensed corporate formation agent
Valid identification of the proposed directors
Certificate of name reservation issuance receipt
Signed alternative name list in case of conflict
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is denied on grounds of deceptive similarity, verify the similarity decision reason and immediately submit the next alternative name on the same application screen. If the rejection is erroneous, file a written objection with the Court Registry within 10 days. A repeated administrative failure may be cured using a new application without losing the existing priority window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Escrow, Deposition of Paid-In Capital, and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, together with a notary public appointed by the Korean Notary Association, typically located in Seoul or the city of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the exact reserved corporate name and deposit the agreed paid-in capital amount. Although Korean law sets no statutory minimum capital, depositing at least KRW 10,000,000 is standard practice to allow a realistic corporate bank account and vendor credit after registration. Obtain a capital deposit certificate (Jabon Bulip Jeungmyeong) from the bank, which serves as irrebuttable proof of payment. Next, appear before a notary public with all founders and directors to certify the Articles of Incorporation. Each subscriber's identity must be verified with a passport or national identity document. The notary must confirm the corporate purpose clause, share types, calculation and payment method of shares, address, and proposed officer list. The executed articles are notarized, and a certified copy is issued. The bank certificate, notarized articles, and escrow details are then assembled for the court registration stage.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Passport or national identity card of each incorporator and initial director
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Bank escrow account opening application
Evidence of capital transfer or deposit
Notary appointment confirmation letter
Consent to appointment of each initial director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the escrow release due to clerical error or insufficient incoming wire details, issue a corrected inbound wire instruction, confirming the beneficiary name exactly as reserved. If the notary public identifies inconsistencies in the Articles, enter into a supplementary notarial document amending the relevant provisions. No funds in the escrow account may be disbursed until the Registry Office completes the legal incorporation registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration of Incorporation with the Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court, or the competent Registry Division of the judicial district where the registered office is situated; e-filing is available via I-Court.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the notarized Articles of Incorporation and escrow certificate, prepare the official Registration Application for Incorporation (Form No. 2). The application must list the trade name, corporate purpose, share capital, head office address, Representative Director, directors, auditor or audit committee, and corporate seal specimen. Submit the envelope to the Court Registry Office together with the notarized Articles, bank certificate, officer acceptance statements, and any court-fixed registration tax receipt. The registry will examine the filings for compliance with the mandatory provisions of the Commercial Act. If accepted, the Registry Office issues the Certificate of Corporate Registration and enters the company into the Commercial Registry. The certificate is indispensable for the subsequent National Tax Service business registration, bank account activation, and manufacturing license filings.
required_dossiers: Registration Application for Incorporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate issued by the Korean bank
Consent letters of the Representative Director and directors
Corporate seal certificate
Proof of registered office leasehold or title ownership
Payment receipt of registration tax and education tax
Corporate identification data of foreign directors if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a written correction order, the company must cure the defect within 14 days by filing a corrective amendment form. If the case is suspended pending an inspector's review of in-kind contributions, engage an independent assessment institute and file the inspector's report. Withdrawal of the original application and refiling a revised application after payment of a second fee is the final curative step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Account Activation at the National Tax Service and Mandatory Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) district office with jurisdiction over the corporate registered address, and Korea Social Security Information Systems for the Four Major Insurances.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after receiving the Certificate of Corporate Registration, file the corporate business registration application with the district NTS office. The application must identify the tax code, business address, representative director, and all anticipated business categories, including medical device manufacturing and wholesale. Provide the corporate seal certificate, copy of Articles of Incorporation, the registry copy, and lease or ownership evidence of the registered office. At the same time, open a full-use corporate bank account by presenting the corporate seal, business registration certificate, director identification, and the resolution of the initial board authorizing the account. The NTS will issue the business registration certificate, which enables the issuance of electronic tax invoices. Enrollment with the Four Major Insurances (national health review, employment insurance, industrial accident compensation, and National Pension) is completed via the Korea Social Security Information Systems portal. The company must also file VAT registration and begin withholding tax remittances for employees.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate
Certificate of incorporation copy issued by the Registry Office
Business registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal specimen certificate
Lease agreement or occupancy certificate for the registered office
Bank account opening authorization letter
Director and shareholder identity documents
Employee roster if staffing has begun
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS returns the application due to incomplete address data or omission of business classification codes, correct the coding and resubmit through the taxpayer web service. Where the business registration certificate is withheld pending a tax office field inspection, permit the inspector access to the registered office and provide all requested books and records within three business days. If the bank refuses account activation, request the NTS certificate and board resolution in writing and escalate to the bank's regional compliance officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Medical Device Manufacturing Establishment License and KGMP Facility Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Medical Device Management Division, through the MFDS regional branch office or the nationwide Integrated Medical Device Information System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for a Medical Device Manufacturing Establishment License under Article 9 of the Medical Devices Act before commencing commercial manufacture of the ECG patient monitor line. The application must include the corporate registration certificate, business registration certificate, a detailed floor plan of the assembly and calibration facility, equipment list, process flow diagram, sterilization or verification methods, test and calibration records for the ECG modules, and a copy of the corporate quality management manual. The MFDS or a designated certification body will conduct a facility audit compliant with the Korean Good Manufacturing Practice (KGMP) standard based on ISO 13485 for medical device production environments. The auditor will verify cleanroom conditions, electrostatic discharge controls, calibration traceability, instrument labeling, complaint handling, and document control. After successful inspection, MFDS issues the Medical Device Manufacturing Establishment License with the assigned medical device registration number. This document remains valid indefinitely but is subject to periodic re-inspection every three years. Production of the ECG device cannot legally be placed on the market before submission and authorization under Article 11 of the Medical Devices Act for the specific device type.
required_dossiers: Medical Device Manufacturing Establishment License application form
Corporate registration certificate
Business registration certificate
Floor plan and facility layout drawings of the assembly line
Equipment schedule and maintenance records
EGC patient monitor product specification and calibration reports
KGMP quality manual and control procedures
Environmental approval registration document for manufacturing facility
Civil defense fire inspection certificate
Resume and qualification certificates of the production supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MFDS issues a deficiency list during the desk review, the applicant must file a supplemental package within 45 days citing the exact corrective action and new documentation. If the facility inspection results in disqualification due to nonconformance in cleanroom or calibration standards, the company must complete corrective and preventive action submissions and request and pay for a re-inspection. In the case of a product-specific denial, correct the technical file and refile after executing the required changes under MFDS guidance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) for the medical device manufacturing establishment license; additionally, the municipal government and Korea Environment Corporation for emission and environmental registration; and the local fire defense district under the National Fire Agency for manufacturing and warehousing fire safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing Establishment License (Approval for Establishment of Medical Device Manufacturer) granted under Article 9 of the Medical Devices Act, supplemented by a KGMP ISO 13485 quality system certificate for the assembly and calibration of bedside ECG telemetry monitors.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, with permit administration through the local municipal environmental permitting office and certification services by the Korea Environment Corporation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Facility Emission Registration (No Full EIA Report Required). The proposed medical device assembly, calibration and warehousing operation is a low-environmental-impact physical facility. It requires only the emission facility registration with the local government under the Clean Air Conservation Act and the Water Environment Preservation Act, provided that the total floor area does not exceed 10,000 square meters and the facility is not located in an exclusion zone. If other chemical equipment using solvent or calibration liquids above 10 tonnes per month is introduced, the tier would escalate to Category 2 requiring an EIA scoping report, and if any treatment facility with air or wastewater emissions at national threshold levels is installed, a full Category 1 EIA Report and public hearing would be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from the calibration and washing process must satisfy Korean Water Environment Conservation Act effluent standards for non-Special large dischargers, with pH within 5.8 to 8.6, biochemical oxygen demand below 80 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand below 80 mg/L, suspended solids below 80 mg/L, and total coliform bacteria limits as prescribed for sanitary wastewater. Volatile organic compound (VOC) concentration at the facility boundary must not exceed 500 µg/m3 on an hourly average, and stack emissions, if any, must comply with the Air Pollutant Emission Standards under the Clean Air Conservation Act. Hazardous waste from solvent waste, used isopropyl alcohol wipes, calibration batteries and electronic scrap must be stored in labeled leak-proof containers, manifested in Korea's Integrated Waste Information System, and transferred only to licensed waste transporters. The facility must also maintain a chemical inventory with safety data sheets and limit all flammable solvent storage to less than 1,000 kg in reinforced fire-proof cabinets with secondary containment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Required clearances include: (a) a Civil Defense and Fire Safety Permit issued by the municipal fire department and the National Fire Agency for the assembled-device warehouse and manufacturing floor, including functional automatic fire extinguishing equipment, emergency exits, ventilation systems in solvent storage areas, and an evacuation certificate for four-story building; (b) a structural load inspection certificate issued by the competent municipal building officer verifying floor loading for heavy ECG monitor packing racks and the calibration chamber; (c) a workplace safety approval issued by the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) after conducting risk assessments covering electrical safety of ECG test rigs, machine guarding for test benches, personal protective equipment for chemical handling, and noise assessment near calibration stations; and (d) if the facility operates an X-ray calibration source, a radiation usage clearance from the Nuclear Safety and Security Commission. No production may commence until the fire certificate and the KOSHA workplace assessment are physically posted on-site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), online via HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (KCS), online via UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr), for export declarations and customs clearance records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory TIN/VAT ID is the 10-digit Korean Business Registration Number issued by the district NTS office through HomeTax. Step 1: determine whether the entity has a Korean domestic place of business for Corporate Tax Act and VAT Act purposes. Step 2: prepare the foreign entity incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation, evidence of the Korean office or permanent establishment, and a written appointment of a local statutory tax representative if the head office is outside Korea. Step 3: file the business registration application in the HomeTax portal (or in person at the competent district NTS office) using the non-resident entity's legal name, domestic place of business address, and representative details. Step 4: after registration, the NTS issues the Business Registration Number, which serves as the Korean TIN and VAT registration number. Step 5: for cross-border trade, register the same Business Registration Number with Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS and obtain a KCS beneficiary/user ID for electronic export declarations. Step 6: if the foreign entity has no domestic place of business but nonetheless makes taxable supplies in Korea, it must still register as a taxable person for VAT before making those supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean domestic tax law does not provide a check-the-box election. A Yuhan Hoesa is automatically taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Tax Act. A foreign corporation may be classified as a domestic or foreign corporation depending on whether its head office or actual place of effective management is located in Korea; no hybrid mismatch or passthrough election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold; mandatory VAT registration from commencement of taxable business in Korea. Simplified taxable person status may lower VAT calculation for qualifying small businesses but does not create a monetary VAT registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates the NTS electronic tax invoice system (E-tax invoice system) under the VAT Act. All VAT tax invoices, including zero-rated export tax invoices, must be issued electronically and transmitted to NTS through HomeTax or an authorized API by the end of the day following issuance. B2C cash receipts are mandated through the NTS cash receipt system for customer-requested or large over-the-counter purchases. There is no per-invoice pre-clearance digital stamping, but NTS validates electronic tax invoice data and maintains a real-time anti-fraud reconciliation ledger for input VAT matching, export declarations, and foreign exchange settlements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean VAT Act, a 0% VAT rate applies to goods physically exported from Korea to a non-resident buyer through a customs export declaration, and to qualifying services supplied for use outside Korea. For the electronic patient monitor/ECG hardware business, zero-rating requires actual shipment of assembled monitors and calibration components out of Korea, transfer of title and risk to the foreign buyer, a valid export declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service, and contemporaneous evidence of export proceeds being settled in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Input VAT incurred on export-related purchases can be refunded through the periodic VAT return once export documentation is retained and substantiated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration accepted through UNI-PASS (electronic export cargo declaration and clearance record)
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the ECG patient monitors, model numbers, quantities, and export value
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight evidencing actual physical departure from Korea
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice showing 0% VAT, the buyer/seller details, and the export declaration reference
Purchase/sales contracts or purchase orders from the non-resident customer
Certificate of export proceeds receipt or foreign exchange settlement confirmation issued by an accredited Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing repatriation of the invoiced export value
NTS E-tax invoice submission receipt for the zero-rated export invoice
KCS export clearance record matched to the goods declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-match export declarations, VAT returns, electronic tax invoices, and bank foreign exchange settlement records. If export zero-rating is claimed without actual shipment, without a valid export declaration, or without receiving export proceeds within the statutory deadline, the NTS reverses the 0% rating, assesses 10% VAT on the supply value, denies related input VAT credits, and may impose additional tax penalties under the VAT Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes, including penalty tax of up to 40% of the underpaid tax. Fraudulent or unverified export zero-rating also exposes the entity and responsible officers to criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with retrospective clawback periods of up to 5 years for ordinary under-reporting and up to 10 years for fraudulent or aggravated tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (as central bank and monetary authority), operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the Foreign Exchange Market Intervention and Capital Flow Management framework
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely convertible capital account with a liberalized current account regime. The KRW is fully convertible for current account transactions such as trade settlements, service payments, and dividend remittances, subject to documentary verification and bank reporting. Capital account transactions, including inbound foreign direct investment, acquisition of domestic securities, and cross-border loans, are freely allowed but require prior or post-event reporting to the designated foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Economy and Finance. There is no general surrender requirement for export proceeds; exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic foreign currency accounts or exchange freely. Profit remittances by foreign-invested companies are permissible subject to presentation of audited retained earnings, tax clearance certificates, and proof of foreign investment registration with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The absence of multiple exchange rates and the existence of an interbank market make the KRW effectively convertible, but banks apply anti-money laundering verification to every cross-border payment. Temporary structural measures may apply during financial stress, however current regulations do not restrict conversion or transfer for legitimate business. Corporate treasurers must still obtain Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation forms, purpose codes, and maintain underlying trade or investment documentation to avoid regulatory sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected within one year from the export date under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and any extension requires prior approval from the designated foreign exchange bank. There is no mandatory conversion ratio or surrender requirement; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a domestic foreign currency account, convert to KRW at prevailing market rates, or use it for approved external payments. Receipts must be declared to the collecting bank, which verifies the underlying export declaration and issues a foreign currency receipt confirmation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions and offshore digital EMI platforms are not viable as primary corporate bank accounts for a South Korean legal entity. Under the Korean Banking Act and Electronic Financial Transactions Act, only licensed domestic banks and authorized foreign exchange banks can provide won and foreign currency accounts to domestic corporations, receive export proceeds, and execute capital account transactions. Offshore EMIs lack a domestic branch license in South Korea and cannot legally issue local IBANs or participate in the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System. They may be used only as supplementary payment wallets for low-value disbursements, but they cannot satisfy statutory capital verification, dividend remittance, or corporate tax payment requirements. Therefore the treasury structure must rely exclusively on domestic Tier-1 banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one authorized signatory or the statutory director must appear physically at the domestic branch for final KYC interview and account activation. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted as a substitute for face-to-face verification for foreign-invested corporations due to AML obligations under the Financial Transaction Reports Act. A power of attorney may be used to authorize a local representative, but the original director must provide biometric verification at a Korean embassy or consulate, and the POA must be notarized and apostilled. Some banks offer video interview for existing customers but still require a physical visit by the local finance officer for document stamping and security device issuance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity from a multi-tiered offshore shareholding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete UBO declaration chart identifying every individual holding 25% or more through the chain; certified copies of share registers and notarized deeds for all intermediate holding companies; corporate registry extracts from the entity's jurisdiction; apostilled certificate of incumbency from the ultimate parent; and sworn affidavits explaining the source of wealth for each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected mismatch between the declared ECG patient monitoring manufacturing scope and the requested payment flows to jurisdictions with high money laundering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts with end customers; proforma invoices and bills of lading; ISO 13485 and medical device quality management certificates; a detailed business activity map showing engineering, component sourcing, assembly, calibration, and logistics sites; and a three-year projected cash flow statement tied to the ISIC 3250 scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient documentation for large inbound capital injections intended as shareholder loans or paid-in capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Notification confirmation issued by the bank or KOTRA; a capital subscription agreement between foreign shareholders and the Korean entity; bank-certified source of funds statements from the remitting financial institution; directors' board resolution authorizing the capital contribution; and a CPA's capital verification report required for statutory capital registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated PEP or sanction-list screening hit on the foreign shareholder or signatory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official government-issued identification and valid passport; independent background verification reports from an internationally recognized due diligence provider; written explanation of any PEP status and a full source of funds declaration; sanctions and enforcement searches across UN, OFAC, EU, and KOFIU lists; and an organizational chart proving the non-sensitive nature of the business relationship.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound foreign direct investments must be registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act by filing an Investment Notification with the designated foreign exchange bank before remittance. The funds should be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the investing company's bank to the Korean entity's capital escrow account held at a Tier-1 Korean bank. The remittance message must include the foreign investment purpose code, typically code 210 for acquisition of shares, and a clear reference to the registered Foreign Investment Report. After the funds arrive, the Korean bank issues a Foreign Currency Receipt Certificate, which is used by a licensed Korean accountant to prepare the statutory capital verification report. No sweep to operating accounts is permitted until the capital verification is completed and the foreign investment registration is updated. Dividends and subsequent loans require separate reporting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for ECG monitor components and finished devices should use SWIFT MT103 for direct telegraphic transfers on ordinary open account terms, or SWIFT MT700 issued and advised letters of credit for higher-value transactions. Documentary collections using SWIFT MT400 and MT202 messages are feasible where trust exists between the Korean entity and overseas buyers. All disbursements must be matched to an export declaration filed through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system, and the remitting bank must verify the foreign exchange transaction code, invoice value, shipping date, and import country documentary evidence. KRW payments to domestic suppliers are cleared through the Bank of Korea's real-time gross settlement system; foreign currency payments are cleared via correspondent banking networks and SWIFT with proper purpose codes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts with authorized Korean banks, with underlying trade invoices or forecast exposure, up to 12 months maturity with real delivery or rollover subject to bank credit limits

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in KRW allowed for non-residents and offshore counterparties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, subject to bank intermediation and reporting when settlement references the onshore KRW rate

Currency swaps permitted with authorized banks for hedging cross-currency capital or trade flows, provided the swap has a confirmed underlying commercial or investment transaction and is reported to the Bank of Korea when entered by resident entities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders; adoption of the balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, statement of cash flows, and allocation of retained earnings, with executed minutes retained in the Minute Book.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting record at the company registered office; National Tax Service (NTS) as an attachment to the corporate income tax return; court registry archive for public corporations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year, on or before March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual general meeting creates director liability and an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million under the Korean Commercial Act; persistent failure to maintain the corporate meeting system may be invoked by creditors as evidence of abandonment, eventually triggering a court-ordered dissolution of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return inclusive of tax adjustment schedules, audited or reviewed financial statements, related-party transaction disclosures, and foreign tax credit slips.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea, via the HomeTax electronic filing system.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following the calendar or fiscal year-end; fiscal-year companies file within three months after the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfounded non-filing penalty of 20% of the unreported corporate tax; under-reporting penalty of 10%; fraudulent omission penalty of 40%; late-payment surcharge of 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount; continuous non-filing leads to forced tax collection, seizure of bank accounts and assets, refusal of business registration certificates, and a court petition for corporate dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local corporate income tax return, which is the local income tax imposed on corporations alongside the national corporate income tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax authority of the registered office jurisdiction, jointly processed through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax system.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax negligence surcharge of 20% for failure to file and 10% for false or deficient reporting; daily late-payment interest of 0.03% on the local tax liability; unpaid local taxes are collected compulsorily and may result in a tax lien, asset seizure, and denial of business permits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: First semi-annual VAT return for January-June, including electronic tax invoices, purchase records, and zero-rate or exempt supply schedules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 of the relevant calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT negligence surcharge of 10% for under-reporting and 40% for fraudulent reporting; additional misstatement penalties apply to inaccurate electronic tax invoices; non-payment surcharge of 0.03% per day; habitual non-filing permits the NTS to order business closure and compulsory restriction of business bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Second semi-annual VAT return for July-December, including annual VAT recalculation and final electronic tax invoice summaries.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same VAT negligence surcharge regime as the first half-year: 10% for under-reporting, 40% for fraud; daily 0.03% late-payment interest; repeated non-filing results in business closure, revocation of business registration, and administrative enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent statutory audit engagement and filing of the certified public accountant's audit report where the compulsory audit threshold is met or where required by lenders, investors, or Korean parent-company reporting obligations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) external audit management archive; National Tax Service (NTS) for attachment to the corporate income tax return; shareholders for availability at the annual general meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Engagement must be concluded before the audit period close; audited financial statements must be adopted and filed no later than March 31 of the following year for calendar-year entities; for KRX-listed public-interest entities, the audit report must be published within one month after the annual general meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor in an audit-mandated company permits the Securities and Futures Commission to appoint an auditor ex officio; criminal and administrative fines up to KRW 30 million can be imposed for obstruction; financial statements lose legal evidentiary value, tax benefits may be denied, and director and auditor civil liabilities attach.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual medical device establishment compliance update, quality management system GMP surveillance report, and post-market monitoring summary for the manufacture and calibration of multi-parameter bedside telemetry monitors classified under ISIC 3250.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Republic of Korea, Medical Device Information System; National Institute of Medical Device Safety Information.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 31 each year for the preceding calendar-year manufacturing, calibration, and post-market surveillance data; any serious adverse event or field safety corrective action is separately reportable within 15 days of occurrence.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MFDS may suspend or revoke the medical device manufacturing establishment license for false or omitted reports; an administrative fine up to KRW 3 million per violation may be imposed; product export and domestic placement are blocked, and license revocation constitutes a forfeiture event causing cessation of manufacturing operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage declaration and insurance-premium settlement report for employment insurance, national health insurance, national pension, long-term care insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service (KOMWEL), National Health Insurance Service (NHIS), and National Pension Service (NPS) via the unified electronic social-insurance filing system.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 30 of the following calendar year for the annual average wage and total wage base declaration; monthly premiums are due by the 10th day of each succeeding month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underdeclaration of the wage base triggers a negligence surcharge of 10% of the omitted premium; default interest of 0.03% per day applies to unpaid premiums; persistent delinquency may exclude the entity from public procurement and may be asserted as a ground for liquidation in bankruptcy proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa is subject to mandatory independent external audit if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, its total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9.2 million. All Korea Exchange listed companies, including KRX, KOSDAQ, and financial-services licensees, are subject to mandatory audit regardless of asset size. No general statutory turnover or employee-count audit trigger exists for ordinary private Korean manufacturing companies; however, a contractual audit covenant, bank facility condition, or designation as a K-IFRS-applying public-interest entity creates an equivalent mandatory audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS for KRX-listed and public-interest companies; K-GAAP under the Korean Accounting Standards for non-listed private companies; simplified SME financial-statement standards may be applied only when no statutory external audit obligation exists.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Korean Commercial Act requires a Register of Members capturing every share transfer and ownership movement. Korea does not maintain a central public UBO return for ordinary private LLCSIG123, but the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information requires the company to identify and document its controllers and material shareholders. Any transfer of shares, change in controlling ownership, or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the statutory registers and reported through the applicable foreign-exchange declaration route within 30 days when a non-resident or foreign-currency transaction is involved. In the annual confirmation cycle, the registered-office agent must obtain a written UBO confirmation signed and dated by the representative director no later than the annual general meeting date; this confirmation is retained in the Minute Book for the statutory seven-year period.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,500 per year for a Seoul or Gyeonggi registered office, corporate secretary, mail handling, statutory register custody, and UBO confirmation services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 per year for a private non-listed Yuhan Hoesa under K-GAAP with a medical-device inventory and telemetry calibration operation; K-IFRS public-interest entity audits generally range from USD 25,000 to USD 80,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive national rates: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested high-tech enterprises may qualify for a 50% reduction for three years and 50% further reduction for two additional years under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; Free Economic Zone and Foreign Investment Zone preferential regimes; R&D tax credits of up to 25% for new-growth-source technology and 50% for SMEs; no general patent box but a hybrid R&D-to-income deduction is available for qualifying in-house intangible development

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return of the Foreign Corporation / Domestic Corporation under the Corporate Tax Act (Form 30 Series) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal (E-filing system)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of the fiscal year end (e.g., December 31 fiscal-year-end filers must file and pay on or before March 31 of the following year); consolidated and special calendar extensions may apply only with proper NTS approval

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, corporate registration number, tax office code, date of incorporation, and head-office address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact Korean-registered legal name of Yuhan Hoesa. For a foreign-invested LLC, state the foreign shareholder’s country of residence and file the NTS 'Foreign Investment Enterprise' schedule to claim treaty and incentive eligibility. Do not use abbreviated names.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business place and enterprise classification: Korean Standard Industrial Classification ('KSIC') code, medical device manufacturing license number, business establishment type, and business operation category
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use KSIC code 3250 (medical instruments) and attach the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety license for the assembly and calibration of multi-parameter ECG telemetry monitors. A foreign-invested company must also declare its B2B trade status and any export-oriented transaction country codes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year coverage, filing type indicator (regular, revised, or defect correction), and number of consolidated or foreign related-party schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark 'Annual Final Return'. If any intercompany sales or royalty payments exceed KRW 10 billion or the Korean NTS’s transfer-pricing reporting threshold, attach supplementary transfer-pricing schedules. Indicate if the Korean entity is a limited risk distributor or entrepreneur under an agreed OECD transfer-pricing method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General ledger accounting income (book net income before corporate income tax provision) computed under K-IFRS or Korean GAAP
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Start with external audit financial statements prepared in Korean won. For non-resident shareholders, eliminate any rebate, marketing support, or intercompany chargeback that lacks an arm's-length benefit test. Reclassify off-book-outlier items to recover the true taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back schedule and tax-mismatch reconciliation: non-deductible expenses, nondeductible bribes/fines, entertainment overlimits, and imputed interest/contributed capital in thin-capitalization cases; subtract non-taxable income and tax-exempt foreign-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back all withheld overseas service fees, funding costs, royalties, and management charges paid to a related foreign shareholder if the payee lacks economic substance. Apply the Korean thin-capitalization rule: interest on debt from a foreign controlling shareholder in excess of 3:1 debt-to-equity will be denied and treated as deemed dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base and loss carryforward: 'taxable income of the fiscal year' after deduction of net operating loss carryover and special reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korea permits a 10-year loss carryforward. The foreign investor must reconcile any permanent establishment ('PE') profit attribution under the Korea DTA; if the shareholder’s residence country has a more favorable PE threshold, the NTS will request an OECD-attributable profit auxiliary return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of final corporate tax liability: application of statutory progressive rates on tax base, deduction of tax credits (R&D, foreign tax credit, minimum tax credit, and local tax surcharge)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply progressive brackets on the resulting tax base. A non-resident parent should credit withheld Korean interest, royalty, and dividend tax received from the Korean sub. Foreign tax credit is capped at the Korean effective tax rate on the foreign-source income. Attach Form C-10 for FTC claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing and anti-avoidance adjustment schedule: transactions with foreign related companies, global profit split, and TP position listings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the section showing all service, royalty, financing, and inventory transactions with foreign related parties; state which of the OECD-approved methods was used (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, or profit split). Non-resident exporters making intercompany sales of the ECG monitors at lower-than-market gross margins will trigger a downward TP adjustment under Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayment reconciliation: interim tax payments, source withholding, and tax paid in foreign jurisdictions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-reference the NTS withholding remittance record for interest, royalties, and dividends paid to the Korean LLC’s non-resident suppliers and shareholders. Any failure to withhold domestic-source income royalty and interest payments attracts a 20% withholding penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of place of effective management and economic substance: number of employees, payroll, office lease, core income-generating activity location, and business assets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty benefits only where the entity is a Korean resident under Article 2 of the OECD Model Convention. The NTS now requests the BOI return showing actual employees in Korea engaged in assembly, calibration, and telemetry software integration. A shell office without personnel or inventory storage will be rejected.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers a non-filing surtax of 20% of the tax payable (40% in the case of fraudulent non-filing); underreporting penalties are 10% if voluntary correction and up to 40% for intentional misstatement; daily delinquency surcharge accrues at 0.022% per day proportional to the overdue days; criminal evasion can lead to imprisonment for up to 6 years under the Special Act for Punishment of Tax Evasion, and the statute of limitation for intentional evasion is 10 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax on gross dividend distributions to non-resident corporate shareholders, increased by 10% local income tax surcharge, yielding an aggregate effective statutory rate of 22%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: File NTS Form W-RE (withholding exemption/reduction request) prior to or within the payment date; obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder’s competent tax authority for the relevant calendar year; execute and file the 'Beneficial Ownership Statement' confirming the dividend recipient is not a conduit, that no back-to-back commitment lowers the passive income, and that the shareholder maintains substantive business activities; submit the payment contract, corporate registration certificate, and board resolution approving the dividend with the NTS district office; if excess withholding is nevertheless levied, lodge an administrative refund claim with the Regional Tax Office within the 5-year statute of limitations, attaching the same TRC and beneficial-ownership evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 20% national plus 2% local income tax surcharge (i.e., 22% aggregate) for outbound royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rates: in the Korea–US DTA, royalties and interest typically qualify for 10%; under many Korean treaties, interest paid to financial institutions is set at 5–10%; royalty treaty rates generally do not fall below 10%, but in certain OECD-aligned treaties a 0% or 15% rate applies. The Korean paying LLC must withhold at the domestic rate unless the payee supplies pre-approved DTA relief forms and a valid beneficial-ownership certificate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in aggregate annual international related-party transactions for the mandatory preparation and filing of Master File and Local File; KRW 100 billion for Country-by-Country Reporting obligation for ultimate parent groups with a Korean constituent entity; smaller thresholds (KRW 5 billion) apply for related-party financial services transactions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Korean taxing authorities apply the Economic Substance Regulation through the 'restriction of Imputed/Inordinate Transactions' rule under Article 66(2) of the Corporate Tax Act, OECD BEPS Actions 3 and 8-10, and the Korean CFC rules under Article 44 of the International Tax Coordination Act. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa claiming the benefit of a tax treaty or free-zone regime must prove sustainable core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Korea, including actual physical premises, qualified employment, and executive decisions to implement, hold, and manage the ECG telemetry patents in Korea; otherwise the NTS will disregard the legal entity and recharacterize profits to the ultimate non-resident principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Fraud / Mispriced Intercompany Sale
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC sells finished multi-parameter ECG monitors to a foreign related-party distributor at a consistently suppressed gross margin, simultaneously paying inflated royalties for the same technology back to a related trademark holder in a no-withholding-tax jurisdiction, leaving no operating profit balance in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may issue a transfer-pricing adjustment under Article 4 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs; the added tax income is recharacterized as a constructive dividend to the parent, with a 20% underreporting surcharge and daily delinquency surcharge applied to the underpaid corporate tax and local income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The NTS will pierce the corporate veil if the director knowingly signs false intercompany contracts and invoices; the director becomes jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and surcharge; criminal proceedings under the Special Act for Punishment of Tax Evasion can impose up to six years’ imprisonment, a fine of up to 30 times the evaded tax, and seizure of personal assets located in Korea and abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa has no actual manufacturing or calibration employees, uses a virtual office address, contracts the entire manufacturing process to an unrelated Korean subcontractor, and passes only paper invoices through Korea solely for the purpose of obtaining the Korean–foreign tax treaty's dividend/royalty benefits while the board is actually managed by a foreign venture-capital except in writing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS denies the beneficial ownership claim under Article 7 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs and under the OECD’s limitation-on-benefits principle, treating the entity as a shell; it re-routes the income ($500,000 of ECG monitor export commission) to the ultimate non-resident shareholder and reclassifies the payments as a constructive dividend, compulsory recomputing profits at 22% withholding plus the ordinary corporate tax penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the shell company personally pay restitution of the understated corporate tax and withheld dividend tax; the Korean court may impose a criminal fine up to 5 billion KRW, prohibit the director from re-entering Korea, and blacklist the director’s personal transit visa; such touch court judgment also permits a Foreign Tax Credit denial and asset seizure of the director’s personal equity in the Korean legal entity.
